subject: Discovery: Data retention & PII handling (FinAnalytics)
messages:
From: Camila Reyes <camila_reyes@redwood.com>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@finanalytics.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 10 Jun 2027 15:05:00 -0700
Subject: Discovery: Data retention & PII handling (FinAnalytics)

Hi Alex -

Thanks again for the call today. Quick recap and next steps so we’re aligned:

- Scope: FinAnalytics wants to surface LLM-powered summaries for customer transcripts (voice/text). Key requirements: 0-retention for raw PII, shortened operational logs, and ability to export audit logs for 90 days.
- Data residency: primary region = us-west.
- Integration: will use Redwood hosted API in a private VPC for initial pilot.

Open items for Redwood to propose:
1) Exact retention windows you need for different log classes (raw transcripts, tokenized request logs, audit logs).
2) Any mandatory 0-retention fields beyond raw transcript (e.g., SSNs, credit card numbers).
3) Procurement timing / legal review owners so we can get a DPA reviewed.

I attached our standard DPA draft (DPA_redwood_v1.pdf) and a simple template you can use to flag exceptions. Can you take a look and confirm the retention windows you need? If you prefer, Rafael (cc'ed) can set up a short call with your privacy lead to walk through technical options (pseudonymization, on-request purge APIs, token-level redaction).

Next steps from our side: Rafael to propose a retention exception schedule and Marissa to include a provisional commercial note in the deal record.

Thanks -

Camila Reyes
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
camila_reyes@redwood.com | (415) 555-0128

Attachment: DPA_redwood_v1.pdf (draft - redlines welcome)

From: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@finanalytics.com>
To: Camila Reyes <camila_reyes@redwood.com>
Cc: Legal - FinAnalytics <legal@finanalytics.com>
Date: Fri, 11 Jun 2027 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Discovery: Data retention & PII handling (FinAnalytics)

Camila -

Thanks for the recap. A few clarifications from our side after syncing with product & legal:

- For raw transcripts that may contain customer PII, we require 0-retention by default. That means transcripts must be deletable immediately after processing and not persist in any logs.
- For request logs (tokenized request metadata), we can accept a short retention window for observability, but need it capped at 7 days and stored in a pseudonymized form (no raw identifiers).
- Audit logs (who accessed what) need to be exportable and retained for 90 days for compliance.

Couple of asks:
1) Can Redwood support an API-based purge we can call after processing to ensure 0-retention?
2) How do you handle KV cache and any disk-backed swapping - are there any cases where PII could persist for longer?

I attached a small spreadsheet (retention-exception-request.xlsx) with our requested mapping so you can propose an implementation.

If we can get written confirmation (even provisional) for the 0-retention and 7-day token logs, we’ll move the DPA to legal review.

Best,
Alex
Senior Product Manager | FinAnalytics
alex.johnson@finanalytics.com
Attachment: retention-exception-request.xlsx

From: Camila Reyes <camila_reyes@redwood.com>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@finanalytics.com>
Cc: Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 11 Jun 2027 14:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Discovery: Data retention & PII handling (FinAnalytics)

Alex -

Thanks - this is helpful. High-level responses to your asks and a proposed exception schedule below. Rafael and I discussed the technical approach and Rafael will follow up with more detail, but I wanted to put the proposed terms in writing so your legal team has something to review.

Proposed retention & controls (provisional):
- Raw transcripts containing PII: 0-retention. Redwood will not persist transcript payloads beyond processing. We will provide an API-triggered purge and a written confirmation procedure for each processed batch.
- Request logs (tokenized metadata): retain for 7 days, stored pseudonymized (no direct customer identifiers). Access limited to support/ops via RBAC and logged in audit.
- Audit logs: retained for 90 days; exportable on request as CSV/S3 delivery.
- KV cache: in-memory first; any disk swap is encrypted and subject to the same purge on our retention schedule. We will provide an architecture note (Rafael attaching) describing implementations and encryption at rest.

Attachments: DPA_redwood_v1.pdf (redlined copy) - please have legal review and mark any sections you need changed. Rafael will attach a short architecture note in a separate email to address the KV cache/disk-swap question.

Next steps:
1) Legal review of DPA + confirmation of the 0-retention clause (we can accept a limited exception schedule documented in the DPA).
2) Rafael to share the architecture note and API purge spec by EOD Monday.
3) Marissa to update the HubSpot deal with a provisional note (I’ve added the related link below).

If that works, we’ll move to procurement.

Thanks,

Camila Reyes
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
camila_reyes@redwood.com | (415) 555-0128

Attachment: DPA_redwood_v1.pdf (redlined)

From: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@finanalytics.com>
To: Camila Reyes <camila_reyes@redwood.com>
Cc: Legal - FinAnalytics <legal@finanalytics.com>
Date: Sat, 12 Jun 2027 10:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Discovery: Data retention & PII handling (FinAnalytics)

Camila / Rafael -

Thanks for the proposed terms. Legal has provisionally accepted the language around 0-retention for raw transcripts and the 7-day token log window, subject to receiving the architecture note and purge API spec. A couple final asks before we start procurement:

- Can you confirm the SOW / deal id you’ll use so procurement can tie the SOW to our PO? (we need the vendor-side reference).
- Please include SOC2 evidence (or access to our security questionnaire) as part of the procurement packet.

If you can send the quick architecture note and the vendor SOW id, I’ll route to procurement and legal and we can aim to start pilot provisioning next week.

Appreciate the quick turnaround.

- Alex
Senior Product Manager | FinAnalytics
alex.johnson@finanalytics.com
